question: Do directly measured clinical FAPI scans establish a new useful imaging phenotype in authenticated EMC, including a meaningful within-patient difference from FDG or clinically relevant lesion detection?
prior_gate: Read original prospective and retrospective FAPI sarcoma/pan-cancer cohorts, case reports, full supplements and citations; identify every eligible EMC patient/lesion/scan and historical label. Seed sources PMC8717183 and JNuclMed2024volume65p880 are leads, not confirmed EMC cohorts; direct JNM page returned403 to root. Refresh discovery beyond them. Prior R3MRI/radiomics/FDG records may be reused; no original FAPI-specific evaluation located in their outcome records.
pilot: Before relevant values, freeze a specific worthwhile contrast and eligibility/measurement/error rules. Verify EMC identity, donors, repeated scans, cohort overlap, tracer identity, uptake timing, scan calibration, paired comparators, treatment/biopsy/scar intervals and lesion verification. Analyze donor-level evidence; multiple lesions are not independent patients. Do not pool differing tracers/SUV protocols as identical or infer values from uncalibrated illustrations. Histological author labels and missing molecular confirmation must remain explicit.
value: A genuinely new, reproducible EMC imaging phenotype could change a prospective imaging experiment. Repeating a published favorable illustration or single already-described result is insufficient. Uptake does not establish tumor-cell localization, therapeutic efficacy, dosimetry or safety.
